title: Keep phones and lights running
summary: Low-power mode, power banks, safe car charging, and how to read battery capacity in watt-hours.

sources.title: Apple Support: Use Low Power Mode to save battery life on your iPhone
CPSC: Winter Storm May Knock Out Power; CPSC Warns of Deadly Carbon Monoxide and Fire Risks

blocks.text: A phone is your alerts, your map and your link to help. Make its battery last.

items: Make a list of everything that needs electricity. Plan batteries or a power bank for each one that matters.
Keep a flashlight for every person. Keep spare batteries.
Keep a battery-powered or hand-crank radio, plus a NOAA Weather Radio with tone alert.
When a storm is forecast, charge your phone, power bank and lights, and consider buying a backup charger.
Ask your medical provider about a power-outage plan for any medical device that needs electricity.

Turn on **Low Power Mode** (iPhone: Settings > Battery > Power Mode, or the battery icon in Control Center). It dims the display, shortens auto-lock to 30 seconds, and stops background refresh, automatic downloads and email fetching.
Not an iPhone? Look in your phone's battery settings for a similar power-saving mode.
Save phone **calls** for emergencies. Phone systems are often busy or down, so send **texts** instead.

blocks.text: Wh tells you how much energy a battery stores. Bigger Wh = more charging.

items: If the pack says mAh, divide by 1,000 to get Ah. Example: 2,500 mAh at 1.2 V = 2.5 Ah x 1.2 V = **3 Wh**.
Use the pack's nominal voltage, which many packs print on the label. Wikipedia's example uses 3.6 V for lithium-ion cells. So 10,000 mAh at 3.6 V = 10 Ah x 3.6 V = 36 Wh.
If the pack already prints a Wh number, use that.
Real usable energy is **less** than the Wh on the label. Some is lost when the pack charges your phone.
To estimate charges: pack Wh divided by your phone battery's Wh. Expect fewer than that. No source gave an exact loss figure, so test your own pack.
Charge from the car **outdoors**. **Never run a car in a closed or attached garage**, even with the door open: it makes CO.
Keep your gas tank at least half full. Gas stations may be closed or without power in an emergency.

blocks.text: Use flashlights or battery-operated candles, not real candles. If you do use a candle, keep it away from anything that burns, never leave it unattended, and put it out when you leave the room and before sleep.
If you depend on a device for health, like a pump or sensor, see the T1D pump and CGM guides for your backup plan.
